links.outcome: Agreement between GPT-5 automated self-evaluation and blinded human clinician ratings
links.effect: GPT-5's self-evaluation results deviated from human judgment, suggesting potential model-based bias in self-assessment.
links.quote: Notably, GPT-5's self-evaluation results deviated from human judgment, exhibiting potential model-based bias.

links.outcome: Inter-rater reliability (QWK) between two blinded dental clinician raters
links.effect: QWK 0.7175 in the prompt search dataset but only 0.1505 in the independent test dataset.
links.quote: Inter-rater reliability was strong in the prompt search dataset (QWK: 0.7175) but lower in the independent test dataset (QWK: 0.1505), reflecting the subjective nature of clinical document assessment; therefore, final human scores were reported as average ratings from two blinded clinicians with bootstrap confidence intervals.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the quality and clinical feasibility of dental-to-medical referral letters generated by three LLMs using expert clinician review, but does not test a specific organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
